R0006.title: False Advertising
R0006.definition: False advertising refers to the practice in commercial activities where operators use advertisements or other methods to make false statements about goods or services that do not match actual content, causing customers or consumers to be misled.
R0006.description: False advertising commonly involves: exaggerating product performance or effects; fabricating customer reviews or usage experiences; marking up prices then offering fake discounts; fabricating sales volumes to create a false impression of popularity; inventing scientific research or data to lend credibility; hiding additional fees; using fraudulent certification labels or awards; making unfair or inaccurate comparisons with competitors; using misleading images or advertisements; and deliberately concealing product defects.
R0006.influence: Consumers are misled into believing products have official endorsements or superior performance, affecting their purchasing decisions.

references.title: Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China

observables: Product detail page copy diverges noticeably from the actual parameters and certification credentials
Product reviews are highly templated and cluster within a short window after listing
The original-price to discount-price comparison is anomalous, with discount depth far exceeding the market norm for similar products
